text:
omar: heads up — canary deploy from last night shows decode p95 ~2.3x higher for short sequences (<=32). noticed after merging dynamic-batcher heuristics PR (#3489).

matt: saw that in the CI perf dashboard too, perf-bot alerted at 03:12. link: https://perf.redwood.local/dashboards/ci/merge-3489

sara: quick numbers from prod-like tests: baseline p95 = 48ms, canary p95 = 112ms, median roughly same. so tail only.

perf-bot: CI perf test failed: decode_path_p95: +135ms (regression threshold 50ms). suspect: KV cache miss amplification + microbatching change.

jen: any flamegraphs or profiles? is this more compute-bound or scheduling?

omar: uploaded a flame to the perf bucket: https://perf.redwood.local/flame/176789. looks like time moved into "sched:stalled_on_kernel_switch" and a new path in "batch_decider::choose_kernel" got hot.

matt: reproduced locally on a 2xA100 canary image. adding perf record shows spikes during attention kernel selection for short-seq workloads, and a lot of short-lived kernels (kickoff overhead).

sara: my hypothesis: batcher now splits microbatches more aggressively; creates more short invocations, which prevents KV-prefetch from amortizing. KV eviction rate jumped ~3x in the canary.

lee: thanks. can you paste the exact git range you suspect? I can bisect.

matt: started git bisect. bad: HEAD (merge PR #3489), good: v1.12.3. narrowed to commit 7f4b2c9 -> 9a1e4d0. suspect change in dynamic-batcher/decision.cc lines where prefetch window shrank.

omar: here's the minimal repro command I used:
```
./run_inference_benchmark --model=gpt-medium --seq_len=16 --batch=64 --reuse_kv=true --warmup=400 --iters=1000
```

jen: if bisect lands on the batcher heuristic, we should consider reverting the specific heuristic and ship a targeted tweak. a full revert of PR #3489 is heavy.

matt: bisect result: 9a1e4d0 (change: reduce_prefetch_window for microbatches). adding a simple patch that restores window for short sequences fixes p95 in local test (48->50ms). patch diff: `diff --git a/batcher/heuristics.cc b/...`

lee: can you attach the tiny patch here? I'll run canary with it.

matt: pasted patch in gist: https://gist.github.com/matt/short-prefetch-fix 
Patch summary: if seq_len <= 32, set prefetch_window = max(prefetch_window, 8) instead of allowing it to be 0. also added a short unit test for eviction rate.

sara: ran quick canary with patch — p95 back to baseline, KV eviction rate normalized. no obvious regressions on long sequences.

omar: ok let's do an emergency canary rollout with the patch only. tagging eng-runtime on the revert PR so SRE can schedule the rollout: @eng-sre please prioritize.

perf-bot: creating rollback candidate: rb/3489-prefetch-fix (CI green so far).

jen: follow-up items: 1) add perf guardrail tests for microbatch short-seq p95, 2) add telemetry for prefetch_window decisions, 3) run a longer soak on canary for 24h.

lee: noted. i'll open a follow-up PR to make the heuristic conservative and add telemetry.

omar: thanks team. after rollback candidate lands, let's monitor p95 and eviction metrics. will update thread with canary timestamps. :thumbsup:

matt: thanks — great catch by CI alerts + quick bisect. :tada:
